subject.title: fix(mcp): avoid memory spikes from oversized client TLS files

question: Should MCP client certificate and key files become unsupported above 64 KiB, or should the bounded reader use a more conservative compatibility limit?
rationale: The implementation mechanism is sound, but selecting the maximum supported certificate-chain and key size changes shipped MCP configuration behavior and cannot be inferred solely from the memory-safety goal.

options.title: Prove and document 64 KiB
options.body: Keep the proposed limit after adding a realistic multi-certificate-chain test and documenting the new failure boundary for upgrades.

options.title: Raise the bounded limit
options.body: Use a larger fixed ceiling that still prevents mistaken multi-megabyte reads while reducing compatibility risk for enterprise certificate bundles.

recommendation.title: Prove and document 64 KiB
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed limit after adding a realistic multi-certificate-chain test and documenting the new failure boundary for upgrades.
